clue.text: Unfrocked monk is not behaving properly

definitions.meaning: a monk thrown out of his religious order is no longer in it
a disorderly person or broken machine is said to be malfunctioning or misbehaving

explanation.surface: A monk who has been defrocked is misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes 'order' as a monastic order; the second is the everyday phrase for misconduct or a breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for unruly conduct, also used of a meeting speaker breaking procedure.

clue.text: Where nurses are posted to the front

explanation.surface: Nurses are being sent to the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means forward, further ahead; split as two words it says on the hospital rooms.

clue.text: For an acrobat, one's highly strung

definitions.text: For an acrobat, one's highly strung

parts.words: For an acrobat, one's highly strung
parts.note: highly strung reads as nervous, but the item meant is literally strung high above the ring for a performer to walk

explanation.definitionFit: A taut wire or cord high above the ground for funambulists to walk along.

clue.text: Universal? Precisely!

definitions.meaning: split up, the phrase means for everyone everywhere
the idiom means exactly, as in looked just like

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means exactly, in every respect; read literally it means for everybody on earth.

clue.text: Give up the burden

definitions.meaning: a burden is the chorus of a song

explanation.definitionFit: To abstain from something, and the repeated chorus of a song or poem, archaically its burden.

clue.text: English side needs a man of quality, and it's pressing

parts.note: a cricket or football side has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals
a gent is a gentleman, a man of good breeding

explanation.surface: The England team needs a classy player, and urgently.
explanation.definitionFit: An urgent or demanding need is one that requires immediate attention.

clue.text: In France, we exhibit common sense

definitions.meaning: practical intelligence, a borrowing from Greek used in British English

explanation.surface: Even in France, the people claim to show good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek word for mind became British slang for practical shrewdness, and it is also the French pronoun for us.

clue.text: Some lights, for instance, turned out — not quite every one

parts.note: lights turned out are switched off

indicators.note: not quite means the word for every one loses its final letter

parts.note: all means every one

explanation.surface: Not quite every light has been turned off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lights' are not lamps but the lungs of slaughtered animals, a classic crossword trick; 'not quite' cuts ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lungs, liver and other organ meats from a butchered carcass are sold as offcuts.

clue.text: Petition is, thus, within the law

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
licit means lawful, the opposite of illicit

explanation.surface: A petition is, therefore, legal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask formally or plead for something is to request it.

clue.text: In a way, fortress we associated with Hood

definitions.text: In a way, fortress we associated with Hood

indicators.note: in a way suggests the letters are taken in another way or arrangement

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's band treated their woodland as a sort of stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of FORTRESS WE and HOOD, joined by 'associated with', are mixed; the whole clue describes the Nottinghamshire woodland of the Robin Hood legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The forest in Nottinghamshire is the legendary home base of the outlaw Robin and his men.

clue.text: Lay back, say, in midst of conflict

indicators.note: the reversed piece sits in the middle of the word for conflict

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: back tells us to turn the abbreviation for say around

parts.note: e.g., for example, is a way of saying 'say'

explanation.surface: Someone is told to lie back, mid-battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay back' looks like an instruction to recline; 'Lay' is the noun or verb for a bet, and 'back' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay money on something is to bet it, a stake placed on an outcome.

clue.text: Opening of film just unpleasant

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so take the start of film

parts.note: just in the sense fair or legitimate, as a rightful claim

explanation.surface: A critic finds the first scenes of a movie merely disagreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' reads as 'merely' but means rightful, deserved.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreadful or awful is extremely disagreeable.

clue.text: Repay insult in letter from abroad one afterwards sent back

indicators.note: sent back tells us the whole string of pieces is read in reverse order

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a foreign letter
the Roman numeral for one
later means afterwards

explanation.surface: An insult arrives in a letter from overseas, and is returned later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insult' belongs to the definition and 'in' is only a link, though the surface makes the insult sit inside a foreign letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike back after an affront is to hit out in return.

clue.text: Store licensed to provide this souvenir

indicators.note: the words store licensed provide the letters, which sit inside them across the word break

explanation.surface: A licensed shop sells keepsakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake or memento of a past time or saint is the item kept.

clue.text: Take up horn and set out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of horn and set are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone picks up a horn and sets off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take up' sounds like taking up an instrument, but a tailor takes up a hem to make it less long.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking up a hem or trousers makes them less long.

clue.text: Allowing little time for consideration

parts.note: though in the sense granting or allowing that
t is the short form of time

explanation.surface: A busy schedule leaves little time to think.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflection or careful thinking about something is the mental act meant.

clue.text: I'd laugh hysterically over lines in ceremonial building

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits over the next one
laughing hysterically is laughing in a wild, disordered way, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: Someone laughs uncontrollably at lines spoken in a grand building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hysterically' scrambles I'D LAUGH into GUILDHA; 'over' puts that above LL in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall where a city's trade guilds or corporation meet, used for civic ceremonies and banquets.

clue.text: Here and now

definitions.meaning: in attendance, as a pupil answering the register
the current moment, as opposed to past or future

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means in attendance; as a noun it is the time going on currently.

clue.text: Air transport using one horsepower

parts.note: one horsepower reads as an engine rating, but is literally a single flying horse carrying riders through the sky

explanation.definitionFit: The winged horse of Greek myth that carried the hero Bellerophon through the air.

clue.text: A lower of strength, in the main

definitions.text: A lower of strength, in the main

parts.words: A lower of strength, in the main
parts.note: plays on a tower of strength; a lower here is something that tows, working at sea, the main

explanation.definitionFit: A small powerful vessel that tows larger ships in and out of harbour.

clue.text: Diaphragm, one doctor inserted in pet

indicators.note: inserted in places the first pieces within the word for a pet

parts.note: a pet is a sulk or huff, as is a miff
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One vet puts a device into an animal's chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' is not an animal: in British English to be in a pet is to be in a sulk, a miff.
explanation.definitionFit: The diaphragm lies across the middle of the torso, the area between chest and waist.

clue.text: Chap attached to university, an American one, for free

parts.note: a chap is a man
MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is a US university

explanation.surface: A man joins a college, an American one, at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attached to' and 'for' are links. 'free' is a verb here, not 'at no charge'.
explanation.definitionFit: To release a slave from bondage is to liberate them.

clue.text: Warning observed, as expected

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
saw means observed

explanation.surface: A warning was noticed, as everyone predicted.
explanation.definitionFit: To have predicted or anticipated something is to have seen it coming.

clue.text: Emotional outburst, with love and exuberant enthusiasm

parts.note: a gust of feeling is a sudden outburst
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A display of feeling, affection and high spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest or relish in doing something is hearty keenness.

clue.text: Shed a little light

definitions.meaning: to drop or let fall, as a liquid
a thin strip of wood or paper used to light a fire or pipe

explanation.definitionFit: To spill something is to let it fall; a spill is also a taper for lighting fires.

clue.text: Pound grew unexpectedly — it might have produced a boom

definitions.text: it might have produced a boom

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters of pound grew turn up in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: Sterling rose suddenly, which might have caused an economic boom.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface boom is economic; the real one is an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: Black powder is an explosive whose ignition makes a loud bang.

clue.text: Old storage area's not full yet

parts.note: still means yet, as in still to come
where there is space left there is room

explanation.surface: An old store-room still has space in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is only a link (has). A still-room was a room in a big house for distilling and storing preserves.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry-like chamber of a large country house where cordials and preserves were kept.

clue.text: They can set you back, blue about marks

indicators.note: back says the assembled letters are read in reverse order
about means the word for blue goes around the letter for marks

parts.note: saxe is a light greyish-blue shade, saxe blue
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Tests can be a setback, leaving you blue about your marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts M inside SAXE to make SMAXE; 'back' turns that round. 'set you back' looks like the definition, but 'back' is needed to turn the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tests are things examiners set candidates, so these are what can be set for you.

clue.text: Disposal of part of Manchester

definitions.meaning: selling something off is disposing of it
a town in the Greater Manchester area of north-west England

explanation.definitionFit: A transaction getting rid of goods for money, and a suburban town south-west of the city of Manchester.

clue.text: Show disapproval about invading country contrary to legislation

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Show disapproval about invading country contrary to legislation (7,3)': WALES reversed (contrary) gives SELAW, but the inserted TATUT is not accounted for by TUT plus 'about' under any standard abbreviation.
annotationWithheld.clue: Show disapproval about invading country contrary to legislation
